vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-2.plain: Prahlada, a boy born into the Asura (demon) family, had been tied up and thrown into the sea with rocks piled on him. Lost in thinking of Vishnu, he became one with him. When he stirred, his ropes broke, the sea and earth shook, and he pushed off the rocks and came out of the water. Then he looked around and remembered that he was Prahlada again.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-3.plain: With his mind and words fully focused, the wise boy Prahlada began praising Vishnu, the Purusha (Supreme Being) who has no beginning. He bows to God as true wisdom, and says God is both things we can see and things we cannot, both with form and beyond form, both beyond words and described in words.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-4.plain: Prahlada keeps praising Hari (Vishnu). He says God holds every quality and is also beyond all qualities. God is tiny and huge, seen and unseen, ugly and beautiful, wisdom and ignorance, cause and effect. All good and bad, and everything that lasts or passes away, comes from God.
themes: making sense of good and bad

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-5.plain: Prahlada bows to Vasudeva (a name of Vishnu), who is both one and many, the first cause of everything, present in all beings and yet beyond them. The sage Parashara, who tells the story, says that as Prahlada sang this, Vishnu, dressed in yellow, suddenly appeared in front of him.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-6.plain: Prahlada stands up in awe and, stammering, keeps saying "Glory to Vishnu." He asks Keshava (Vishnu) to bless and purify him. Vishnu says he is pleased with Prahlada's steady love and offers him any wish. Prahlada asks only that his faith never grow weaker, through all his future lives.
themes: asking God for strength of faith

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-7.plain: Prahlada asks that his love for God be as strong as the hold ordinary people's possessions have on them. Vishnu says Prahlada already has this love and always will, and asks him to choose another wish. Prahlada asks God to forgive his father for the wrong he did in punishing him for praising God.
themes: praying for someone who hurt you

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-8.plain: Prahlada lists what his father did to him: attacked him with weapons, threw him in fire, had snakes bite him, poisoned his food, and threw him tied up into the sea under rocks. Still, he asks Vishnu to free his father from the guilt of these acts. Vishnu agrees and offers him yet another wish.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-9.plain: Prahlada says he already has everything he wants, because his faith will never fade. He says that someone with firm love for God can have wealth, goodness, pleasure, and even freedom from rebirth. Vishnu tells him that because of his steady love, he will reach final freedom.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-10.plain: After Vishnu disappears, Prahlada goes back and bows to his father. His father, in tears, hugs him and asks, "My child, are you alive?" He is kind to him and regrets what he did. Prahlada then lovingly takes care of his father and his teacher.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-11.plain: Later, after Vishnu killed his father in the form of the man-lion (Narasimha), Prahlada became king of the Daityas (demons). Because he was good, he ruled with great wealth and had many children. When his rule ended, through meditation on God, he gained final freedom from being born again.

vishnu-purana-vamana-3-1-1.plain: In a later age, Vishnu was born as Vaikuntha to Vikunthi. In the present age he was born as Vamana, the dwarf son of Kashyapa and Aditi. With three giant steps he won back the worlds and gave them to Indra (Purandara). In each age a form of Vishnu protects all beings.

vishnu-purana-vamana-3-1-2.plain: He is called Vishnu because his power fills and enters the whole world; the name comes from a root meaning "to enter." All the gods, the Manus (first rulers of each age), and the kings of gods are just forms of Vishnu's power.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-1.plain: One day young Krishna went to the forest of Vrindavana without his brother Balarama, wearing flower garlands and surrounded by cowherd boys. He went to the sparkling Kalindi (Yamuna) river and found a pool where the terrible serpent Kaliya lived, its water boiling with poison.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-2.plain: The poison had withered the big trees on the shore and burned birds touched by the spray. Seeing the serpent, as frightening as death itself, Krishna thought: this is the wicked snake Kaliya, whom I defeated and forced to leave the ocean.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-3.plain: Krishna thinks: this serpent has poisoned the Yamuna river, so the thirsty cows and herders cannot drink. He decides to defeat it so the people of Vraja can live happily without fear. He says he came to earth to punish the wicked, so he will climb a Kadamba tree and jump into the pool.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-4.plain: Krishna tightens his clothes and boldly jumps into the serpent's pool. The lake churns, and the poisoned spray sets distant trees on fire until the whole sky seems to blaze. In the water, Krishna slaps his arms loudly to challenge the serpent.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-5.plain: Hearing the noise, the serpent king Kaliya comes out with copper-red eyes and hoods flaming with venom. Many other poisonous snakes and richly adorned serpent-women come with him. They wrap around Krishna and bite him with fiery, poisonous fangs.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-6.plain: Seeing Krishna wrapped by snakes, his friends run back to the village crying that he foolishly jumped into Kaliya's lake and is being eaten. The news hits like thunder, and the cowherds and their wives, led by Yashoda, Krishna's mother, rush to the lake.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-7.plain: The women cry out, confused, "Where has Krishna gone?" Yashoda hurries, stumbling with fear. Balarama, Nanda (Krishna's father), and the cowherds reach the river and see Krishna motionless in the serpent's coils. Nanda and Yashoda are frozen with shock at the sight of their son.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-8.plain: The grieving women say they will follow Yashoda into the lake and will not return home without Krishna. They ask what a day is without the sun or a night without the moon; their village without Krishna would be like a pond with no water.
themes: can't live without a loved one

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-4.plain: The priests tell Prahlada to stop praising Vishnu, his family's enemy, because a father is the highest teacher. Prahlada politely agrees that his family is famous, that his father earned his high place, and that a father deserves the most respect.
themes: pressure to give up your faith

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-5.plain: Prahlada says he truly respects his father and has done nothing wrong there. But he questions their claim that there is no need to seek shelter in the eternal God. He stays quiet for a while out of respect, then smiles and asks if that was a fair thing to say.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-6.plain: Prahlada explains that people want four things in life: goodness, fulfilled desires, wealth, and freedom from rebirth. Since God is the source of all four, worshipping him is not pointless. Great sages like Marichi and Daksha gained these things this way.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-7.plain: Prahlada adds that others, through true wisdom and meditation, came to know God and were freed from the cycle of worldly life. Worshipping Hari (Vishnu) with a united, focused mind is the root of wealth, honor, wisdom, children, goodness and freedom.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-8.plain: Prahlada humbly says they are his teachers and his understanding is small. The priests threaten him: if he does not give up these ideas, they will perform rituals to kill him. Prahlada asks who can really kill or save anyone.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-9.plain: Prahlada says each person destroys or protects himself by doing evil or good. The angry priests use magic to create a terrifying fiery woman, who stabs Prahlada in the chest with a spear, but the spear breaks into a hundred pieces.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-10.plain: The narrator explains that even a thunderbolt would shatter against the chest of someone who keeps Hari (Vishnu) in his heart, so a spear could do nothing.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-11.plain: The evil magic turns back on the priests and burns them to death. Seeing them burn, Prahlada cries out to Krishna, the creator present everywhere, and begs him to save these same priests who tried to kill him.
themes: compassion for those who hurt you

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-12.plain: Prahlada prays that since Vishnu lives in all beings, the priests should come back to life. He says he never hated anyone who tried to kill him, whether by poison, fire, elephants or snakes, and if that is true, the priests should live again.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-13.plain: At his touch the priests rise up unhurt. They bless the humble boy with long life and strength, then go tell the king everything.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-1.plain: Hearing that the priests' magic failed, King Hiranyakashipu calls Prahlada and asks where his amazing power comes from: training, magic, or birth.
themes: where does inner strength come from

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-2.plain: Prahlada bows to his father and says his power is not magic or natural; it is easy for anyone with God in their mind. Someone who wishes no harm and treats everyone like himself has no cause for suffering, but one who hurts others in deed, thought or word plants seeds of misery.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-3.plain: Prahlada says he wishes, does and speaks no evil to anyone, and always meditates on Keshava (Vishnu) who lives in all beings. Since God is in every creature, wise people should love all creatures.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-4.plain: Furious, the king orders his servants to throw Prahlada from his enormously tall palace onto the mountain rocks. They throw him down, and he falls thinking of Hari (Vishnu).

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-5.plain: Mother Earth catches the falling boy, and he is unhurt with no broken bones. The king then asks Samvara, an expert in magic spells, to kill him.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-6.plain: Samvara boasts of his thousands of magic tricks and attacks Prahlada. Prahlada stays calm, holds no hatred even for Samvara, and meditates on Vishnu, the slayer of the demon Madhu.
themes: calm in the face of attack

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-7.plain: Vishnu sends his blazing discus, Sudarshana, to protect Prahlada, and it destroys all of Samvara's illusions.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-8.plain: The king orders a deadly, freezing wind to kill Prahlada, and it enters his body. Prahlada thinks of Vishnu, and Vishnu, present in his mind, drinks up the wind, which is destroyed.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-9.plain: With all attacks defeated, Prahlada goes back to his teacher, who teaches him every day the science of government written by Usanas (Shukra, teacher of the demons) for kings.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-10.plain: The teacher tells the king that Prahlada has mastered politics and is humble. The king asks Prahlada how a king should treat friends and enemies, and what to do when advancing, retreating, or at peace.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-5.plain: Autumn cleared the clouds from the sky, dried the mud and made the waters clear again. The poet compares this to how deep focus pulls the mind away from things the senses chase. The lake filling, staying still and then going down is compared to breathing in, holding the breath and breathing out in yoga practice.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-6.plain: In autumn Krishna went to Vraja, the cowherds' village, and saw everyone busy getting ready for a festival for Sakra (another name for Indra, king of the gods). Krishna was very wise, but he asked the elders, as if just curious, what this festival was and why they were so happy about it.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-7.plain: A cowherd kindly explains that Indra, king of the gods, rules the clouds and rain. Rain grows the grain that feeds people and lets them make offerings to the gods. Rain also keeps the cows healthy, so they have calves and give milk.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-8.plain: The cowherd continues: wherever rain falls, crops grow and nobody goes hungry. Indra draws water up from the earth through the sun's rays and pours it back down as rain for everyone. That is why kings and ordinary people all honor Indra with offerings when the rainy season ends.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-9.plain: Parashara, the sage telling this story, says Krishna (here called Damodara) answered his foster-father Nanda in a way meant to make Indra angry. Krishna says: we are not farmers or traders, we live in the forests, and cows are our gods. He then begins to explain the practical knowledge of how people earn a living.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-10.plain: Krishna says there are three ways of making a living: farming, trading and raising cattle. Farmers live by farming, traders by trade, and the cowherds live by tending cows. So whatever actually supports a person should be what they honor most, because it is what helps them.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-11.plain: Krishna says a person who worships someone else's god while living from his own does not do well in this life or the next. He describes the cowherds' world: past the farms is forest, and past the forest are hills. They have no walls, fields or houses, and they travel happily wherever they like in their wagons.
themes: being true to your own way

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-12.plain: Krishna says they have heard that the mountain spirits take any shape and roam the woods. If angry with forest people, they can become lions or wild beasts and kill them. So the cowherds should honor the mountains and their cattle, not Indra, because cattle and mountains are their true gods.
themes: honoring the land you live on

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-14.plain: Krishna suggests that after making the offerings and feeding the Brahmins (priests), the cowherds should walk in a circle around the cows, which are decorated with autumn flower garlands. If they do this, they will win the favor of the mountain and of himself.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-15.plain: When Nanda and the other cowherds heard Krishna, their faces lit up with joy. They agreed he had spoken well and said they would do just as he said and worship the mountain.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-16.plain: The people of Vraja worshipped the mountain with offerings of curds, milk and meat. They fed thousands of Brahmins and guests, just as Krishna had said. Then they walked around the cows and the loudly bellowing bulls.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-17.plain: On top of Govardhan Hill, Krishna appeared as the mountain, said "I am the mountain" and ate the food the cowherds offered. At the same time, in his usual form, he climbed the hill with the cowherds and worshipped this other form of himself. The mountain-form promised many blessings and vanished, and everyone went home.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-1.plain: Parashara tells his student Maitreya that Indra, angry at losing his offerings, called the great storm clouds. He ordered them to obey without question and to punish Nanda and the cowherds, who trusted Krishna, by hurting their cattle with wind and rain. Indra said he would ride his huge elephant and help make the storm stronger.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-2.plain: Following Indra's command, the clouds came down in a terrible storm of wind and rain to destroy the cattle. The rain was so heavy that earth, sky and horizon seemed to blend into one. The clouds thundered and poured without stopping.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-3.plain: Rain poured day and night, darkness covered the earth, and water was everywhere. The cows shrank down in fear or died. Some shielded their calves with their bodies, others watched their calves swept away, and the shivering calves looked to their mothers or moaned as if calling to Krishna for help.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-4.plain: Krishna (here called Hari) saw the whole village of Gokula terrified, people and cattle alike. He knew Indra caused this out of anger at losing the offerings meant for him. He decided it was his duty to protect the village, and planned to lift the mountain and hold it like a giant umbrella over them.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-5.plain: Krishna lifted Govardhan Hill with one hand as easily as if playing. He told the cowherds to hurry under it, where they would be safe from the wind and rain, and not to fear that the mountain would fall.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-6.plain: All the people, soaked by the rain, came under the mountain with their cattle, wagons and belongings. Krishna held it steady over their heads. They gazed at him with joy and wonder and sang his praises.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-11-7.plain: For seven days and nights Indra's clouds poured rain on the village, but the mountain kept everyone safe. Defeated, Indra told the clouds to stop. When the sky cleared, the people went home, and Krishna, while they watched in amazement, put the mountain back in its place.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-41.plain: Indra keeps praising Sri (Lakshmi, goddess of fortune and Vishnu's wife). He says only she can live with Vishnu. When she left, the three worlds almost fell apart, and her return saved them. Every good thing people have, like family, friends, homes, food and money, comes from her kind look.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-42.plain: Indra says that health, wealth, victory over enemies and happiness come easily to people Sri looks upon. She is the mother of all beings, just as Vishnu (Hari) is their father. Together they have filled the whole universe from the start.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-43.plain: Indra admits that without Sri nothing is safe: not money, animals, houses, clothes, bodies, family or friends. He says a person she abandons also loses goodness, truth, purity and good character.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-44.plain: Indra says that people Sri looks upon become respected, wise, brave and admired, even if they had no special qualities before. People she turns away from lose their good qualities at once. Even the gods cannot describe all her greatness. He ends by begging her never to leave him.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-45.plain: The sage Parashara tells how Sri, pleased with Indra's hymn, offered him any wish. Indra (also called Satakratu) asked first that she never leave the three worlds again.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-46.plain: Indra's second wish is that Sri never abandon anyone who praises her with this same hymn. Sri agrees to both wishes. She promises never to leave the three worlds and never to be displeased with anyone who chants the hymn.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-47.plain: Parashara explains to his student Maitreya that Sri was first born as the daughter of the sage Bhrigu and his wife Khyati. Later she came up out of the ocean when the gods churned it. Whenever Vishnu (Janardana) is born in a new form on earth, Sri is also born to help him.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-48.plain: Sri always takes a form that matches Vishnu's. When he came as the dwarf Vamana, she came as a lotus. With Parasurama she was the Earth, with Rama she was Sita, and with Krishna she was Rukmini. If he is a god she is a goddess, and if he is human she is human.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-1.plain: Parashara begins the story of the wise boy Prahlada. Long ago, Prahlada's father, the demon king Hiranyakashipu, was proud of a gift of power from the god Brahma. With it he conquered the three worlds. He took over Indra's throne and did the jobs of the sun, the wind, the waters, fire and the moon.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-2.plain: Hiranyakashipu also made himself lord of wealth and of death. He took all the offerings meant for the gods. The frightened gods fled their heaven and hid on earth disguised as humans. Proud and rich, the demon king enjoyed every pleasure he wanted while singers praised him.
themes: forced to hide out of fear

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-3.plain: All the heavenly beings had to worship Hiranyakashipu, who loved to drink. They sang, played music and cheered for him. Heavenly dancers performed while he drank in his crystal palace.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-4.plain: Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada was a young boy living at his teacher's house, learning his lessons. One day the teacher brought him to his father, who was drinking. The father lifted the bowing boy up and asked him to repeat the main thing he had learned.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-5.plain: Prahlada says that what fills his thoughts is this: he bows to the Supreme Being. That Being has no beginning or end, never grows or shrinks, and is the cause of everything. Hearing this, his father turns red with rage and shouts at the teacher, "What is this, wicked Brahmin?"
themes: standing up for what you believe

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-6.plain: The king accuses the teacher of teaching his son to praise his enemy Vishnu. The teacher says he did not teach it. When the king asks Prahlada who taught him, the boy says Vishnu himself is the teacher of the whole world and lives in everyone's mind.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-7.plain: Prahlada asks who else could teach us but Vishnu. The furious king demands to know who this Vishnu is. Prahlada says Vishnu is the great God whom devoted people meditate on, whose glory words cannot describe, who is everything and from whom everything comes. The king shouts, "While I live, who else do you call supreme lord?"
themes: pride that cannot accept a higher power
calm courage before an angry parent

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-8.plain: The king threatens Prahlada with death. The boy calmly says Vishnu is the creator, protector and lord of every creature, including his father. He asks his father not to be angry. The king thinks some evil spirit has taken over his son.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-9.plain: Prahlada says Vishnu is not only in his mind but fills the whole universe and guides everyone, even his father. The king orders the boy taken back to his teacher to be controlled. He thinks someone wicked must have taught him to praise his enemies.
themes: parents trying to change a child's beliefs

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-10.plain: Prahlada goes back to his teacher and keeps studying and serving him well. Much later his father calls him again and asks him to recite a poem. Prahlada recites a prayer to Vishnu, the source of matter, souls and all creation.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-11.plain: Enraged, the king orders his son killed, calling him a traitor to his family. Thousands of demons (Daityas) come with huge weapons. Prahlada tells them that Vishnu is present in their weapons and minds too, so the weapons will not hurt him.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-12.plain: The demons attack, but Prahlada feels no pain and his strength keeps returning. His father promises to spare him if he stops praising Vishnu. Prahlada says he feels no fear, because Vishnu is in his mind, and just remembering Vishnu removes all dangers and the sufferings of life.
themes: pressure to give up your beliefs

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-11.plain: Hiranyakashipu, the demon king, tests his son Prahlada on how to rule. He asks how a king should treat ministers, spies, subjects and enemies, when to make peace or war, how to build forts and how to stop rebellions.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-12.plain: Prahlada bows humbly and says he has learned all these lessons from his teacher, but he does not agree with all of them. Kings are taught four ways to handle friends and enemies: kind words, gifts, punishment and turning people against each other. But Prahlada gently says he sees no one as a friend or an enemy.
themes: seeing no one as an enemy

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-13.plain: Prahlada explains why. Vishnu, also called Govinda, lives in his father, in Prahlada himself and in every creature. So it makes no sense to divide people into friends and foes.
themes: seeing others as connected to you

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-14.plain: Prahlada says studying ways to beat enemies is tiring and useless, because it rests on false ideas. It is better to learn about one's own true self. Only ignorance mistakes ignorance for knowledge, just as a small child thinks a firefly is a real fire.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-15.plain: Prahlada says real action is what frees us from being trapped in worldly life. Real knowledge is what leads to that freedom. Everything else only wears us out or makes us clever at a skill. He offers to tell his father what truly helps, and points out that everyone wants power and money.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-16.plain: Prahlada says wealth and kingdoms come from good deeds done in past lives, not from hard effort alone. Even foolish or cowardly people sometimes become kings by fate. So anyone who wants greatness should try to be good and devoted.
themes: being good instead of chasing status

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-17.plain: Prahlada says anyone seeking final freedom should look on all beings equally. Gods, people, animals, birds and snakes are all different forms of Vishnu. Whoever truly understands this sees the whole world as one with himself, and Vishnu, who removes all suffering, is pleased with him.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-18.plain: Parashara, the sage telling this story, says Hiranyakashipu jumps up in fury and kicks his son in the chest. He orders his demon chiefs to tie the boy up with snakes and throw him into the ocean. He fears others will start following Prahlada's beliefs.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-19.plain: The king complains that Prahlada keeps praising Vishnu, his enemy, no matter how often he is stopped. The demons tie Prahlada with ropes and throw him into the sea. The ocean shakes and rises in huge waves, and the land is about to flood, so the king gives a new order.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-20.plain: Hiranyakashipu orders the demons to pin the boy under the sea with rocks. He lists every attack Prahlada has survived: fire, weapons, snakes, poison, deadly wind, magic, falls from mountains and the elephants that guard the sky. He calls his son a constant source of misery.
themes: a parent who rejects his child

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-21.plain: The demons pile rocks over Prahlada for thousands of miles. Lying at the bottom of the sea, he stays calm and begins to praise Vishnu, calling him the lotus-eyed one and the soul of all worlds.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-22.plain: Prahlada keeps praying. He honors Vishnu as Krishna and Govinda, the friend of priests and cows, and the helper of the world. Vishnu creates the universe as Brahma, protects it, and destroys it at the end of an age as Rudra (Shiva).
themes: God as creator, protector and destroyer

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-23.plain: Prahlada says Vishnu, called Achyuta (the one who never falls), is the source of everything. That includes gods, demons, people, animals, plants, stones, the elements, the senses, the mind, time and nature. All of these are his forms.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-24.plain: Prahlada says Vishnu is both knowledge and ignorance, truth and untruth, poison and nectar. He is every action, the one who receives its results, and the reward of every good deed. He is in Prahlada, in others, and everywhere in the universe.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-25.plain: Prahlada says monks meditate on Vishnu and priests offer sacrifices to him. The whole universe is his largest form. His smallest, most hidden form is the soul inside every being.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-26.plain: Prahlada praises an even higher Supreme Soul in Vishnu. It lies beyond the individual soul and cannot be sensed or imagined. He bows to this highest form, called Purushottama (the Supreme Person), the soul of all creatures.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-27.plain: Prahlada bows to the divine power that the senses, words and mind cannot reach. Only the truly wise can know it. He salutes Vasudeva (Vishnu), who is part of everything yet also beyond everything, and who has no name or form.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-28.plain: Prahlada says even the gods cannot see Vishnu's true form, so they worship his forms on earth. Vishnu lives in every mind and sees all the good and bad people do. Prahlada asks this Vishnu to be pleased with him.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-19-29.plain: Prahlada asks Hari (Vishnu) for mercy and says the universe is woven through him like cloth. Then he goes deeper and declares that Vishnu is also himself. He feels he is one with the eternal Spirit, from which all things come.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-20-1.plain: Parashara says that as Prahlada meditated on Vishnu as one with himself, he lost all sense of being a separate person. He felt he was the endless, eternal Supreme Soul. Because his mind was now pure, Vishnu appeared within it.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-1.plain: The sage Parashara begins telling Maitreya how Sri (Lakshmi, goddess of good fortune) came to be lost and found. Durvasa, a wild, hot-tempered sage who was a form of Shiva, was wandering the earth. He saw a heavenly garland in the hand of a Vidyadhari, a female sky-spirit, and asked her for it.
themes: a sage asks for a gift

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-2.plain: The Vidyadhari bowed respectfully and gave Durvasa the garland. He put it on his head and kept wandering. Then he saw Indra, king of the gods and husband of Sachi, riding his huge elephant Airavata with the other gods.
themes: meeting the king of the gods

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-3.plain: Durvasa took the sweet-smelling garland, which drew swarms of bees, and threw it to Indra. Indra did not wear it. He put it on his elephant's head, where it looked like the Ganges river flowing on Mount Kailasa.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-4.plain: The elephant was dazed by the strong smell. He sniffed the garland with his trunk and threw it on the ground. Durvasa grew furious and called Indra wicked, proud and drunk on his wealth.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-5.plain: Durvasa says Indra should have bowed, thanked him gladly and worn the blessed garland. Because Indra did not, Durvasa curses him to lose his heavenly good fortune. He accuses Indra of thinking himself too great and treating him like any ordinary priest.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-6.plain: Durvasa adds that because Indra threw his gift to the ground, all three worlds will lose their good fortune. He reminds Indra that all living things fear him when he is angry, yet Indra insulted him out of pride.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-7.plain: Indra quickly got off his elephant and humbly begged Durvasa's pardon. Durvasa refused. He said he was not gentle or forgiving like other sages such as Gautama, whose praise had only made Indra proud.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-8.plain: Durvasa says the praise and kindness of sages like Vasishtha made Indra vain enough to insult him. He says nobody can face his angry face and fiery matted hair without fear. He will not forgive, so Indra's pleading is useless.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-9.plain: Durvasa left, and Indra rode back to his city, Amaravati. From then on the three worlds lost their good fortune and their glory faded. Sacrifices and healing plants grew weak, and people stopped worshipping, practicing self-discipline and giving to charity.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-10.plain: People became weak and were ruled by their desires. They could not control themselves even in small things. The passage explains that strength and prosperity go together. Without them goodness fades, and those without power and wealth are pushed around by everyone.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-11.plain: People who are overpowered lose their good sense. With the worlds weakened, the Daityas and Danavas, demon enemies of the gods, were driven by greed. They began to attack the gods.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-12.plain: The demons defeated Indra and the other gods. Led by Agni, the fire god, the gods went to Brahma, the creator and grandfather of all, for protection. Brahma answered them.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-13.plain: Brahma tells the gods to seek shelter with Vishnu. Vishnu is the supreme Lord who creates, protects and ends all things. He defeats the demons and removes the suffering of the humble. Brahma promises Vishnu will help them.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-14.plain: Brahma led all the gods to the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk. There he praised Vishnu, also called Hari, with beautiful words.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-15.plain: Brahma praises Vishnu, also called Narayana, as the Lord of everything. He is endless and never born, and he holds up the worlds. He is smaller than the smallest thing and greater than the greatest. All things come from him, and yogis meditate on him to be set free. He is beyond the qualities of nature.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-16.plain: Brahma prays for Vishnu's kindness. He calls Vishnu the purest of all and the first Being. He says Vishnu is not limited by time, even its tiniest units. Vishnu is the soul in every body, and he is both the cause and the result of everything.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-17.plain: Brahma bows to Vishnu as the cause behind every cause and the result of every result, all the way down. Vishnu is both the maker and what is made.
themes: God as the source of everything

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-18.plain: Brahma bows to Vishnu's highest state, which is pure awareness. It is eternal, never decays and has no cause. It is neither large nor tiny and cannot be divided. All the energy of the universe rests in just a tiny fraction of him.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-19.plain: Brahma says that not even the gods, the sages, he himself or Shiva (Sankara) fully know Vishnu's highest state. Dedicated yogis glimpse it through the sacred sound Om once their good and bad deeds are used up. Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva are all forms of his power.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-20.plain: Brahma begs Vishnu, the refuge of all, to be kind and show himself to his devotees. The gods then bow too. They ask Vishnu to appear and praise him as present in everything, a state even Brahma cannot fully know.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-13.plain: The demon king Hiranyakashipu orders deadly snakes to kill his son Prahlada. The snakes bite him all over, but Prahlada keeps his mind happily fixed on Krishna (Vishnu) and feels nothing.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-14.plain: The snakes tell the king that their own fangs broke and their hoods burned, yet the boy's skin has no wound. The king then orders the giant elephants that guard the directions of the world to crush Prahlada. He says one's own children can sometimes destroy a family, like fire burning the wood it comes from.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-15.plain: The huge elephants throw Prahlada down and stab at him, but their tusks break against his chest while he remembers Govinda (Vishnu). Prahlada tells his father this is not his own strength. It happens because he called on Janardana (Vishnu), who removes all danger and sin.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-16.plain: The king orders his demons to build a huge fire around Prahlada and has the wind god fan it. Prahlada says the fire does not burn him. To him everything around feels cool, like being among lotus flowers.
themes: peace in the middle of danger

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-17.plain: The family priests, descendants of the sage Bhargava, ask the king to calm his anger against his own son. They promise to train the boy so that he becomes obedient and helps fight the king's enemies, the gods.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-18.plain: The priests say the boy's behavior comes from being young and ask the king to let go of his anger. If Prahlada still will not give up worshipping Hari (Vishnu), they will find a sure way to kill him. The king agrees and has his son pulled out of the fire.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-19.plain: Back at his teacher's house, Prahlada secretly teaches the other demon boys whenever he can. He tells them he wants nothing from them. He reminds them that every creature is born, grows up, grows old, and then dies.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-20.plain: Prahlada says they have all seen this cycle with their own eyes. Whoever dies is born again, as the holy books teach. Each birth comes from good and bad deeds done before, and every stage of life involves pain.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-21.plain: Prahlada says foolish people think that easing hunger, thirst or cold is true pleasure, but it is only a short break from pain. He adds that the body is made of fluids and flesh, so its beauty and charm do not last.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-23.plain: Prahlada says rich people always worry that their things will be lost, burned or stolen. Being born, dying and entering a womb again are all painful. So the world is full of suffering, and Vishnu is the only safe shelter in it.
themes: the world feels full of suffering

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-24.plain: Prahlada tells the boys not to think they are too young for this, because the soul inside them never dies. Only the body is young or old. He describes how people keep putting off spiritual effort: a child waits for youth, a young person waits for old age. Then in old age their senses fail, and they regret doing nothing when they could.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-25.plain: Prahlada says people want true knowledge but get distracted by empty hopes. They play in childhood and chase worldly things in youth, and suddenly old age arrives. So a person should work for the soul's good right now, even as a child.
themes: don't wait until it's too late

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-26.plain: Prahlada says that even if they doubt him, they should simply think of Vishnu, who frees beings from bondage. Remembering Vishnu is easy, and it brings good fortune and removes sins. If their minds rest on Him day and night, they will be able to laugh at every trouble. He notes the whole world suffers from three kinds of pain: from the body and mind, from other beings, and from nature and fate.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-27.plain: Prahlada asks why anyone wise would hate others, since all beings deserve kindness. If others are richer or happier, we should be glad for them instead of jealous, because letting go of spite is a reward in itself. The wise even pity people who hate their enemies, because such people are confused.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-28.plain: Prahlada says he has given reasons to stop hating, even if we treat ourselves as separate from others. But the deeper truth is that the whole world is Vishnu, who is present in every being. So wise people see no real difference between themselves and anyone else.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-29.plain: Prahlada urges the boys to give up the angry ways of their demon family. Instead they should seek a perfect happiness that no god, demon or other being can take away. Disease, hatred and desire cannot disturb it either.
themes: peace that cannot be taken away

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-17-30.plain: Prahlada says pure, endless happiness comes to anyone who fixes the mind on Keshava (Vishnu), and worldly life will never truly satisfy. Treating all creatures equally is itself the worship of Vishnu. When Vishnu is pleased, wealth and pleasure seem small. He tells them to turn to the tree of true wisdom and enjoy its fruits.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-1.plain: The frightened demons tell the king that Prahlada is teaching his beliefs to the other boys. Hiranyakashipu orders his cooks to secretly poison all of Prahlada's food, and they do so.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-2.plain: Prahlada repeats Vishnu's name and eats the poisoned food. It does him no harm in body or mind, because the holy name defeats the poison. The scared cooks report to the king that his son digested the deadly poison.

vishnu-purana-prahlada-1-18-3.plain: The king orders the priests to perform rituals that will destroy Prahlada. The priests first speak gently to him. They remind him he comes from Brahma's famous family and is the king's son, and ask why he relies on the gods when his own father is everyone's protector.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-21.plain: After Brahma and the gods finish their prayer, the divine sages led by Vrihaspati (teacher of the gods) also praise Vishnu. They call him the first being, the creator, the one honored in every sacrifice and the lord of past and future. They humbly ask him to show himself to them.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-22.plain: The sages point out all the gods who have come to Vishnu: Brahma, Shiva (Trilochana, the three-eyed one) with the Rudras, the Sun, Fire, the Ashvin twins, the Vasus, the Maruts and Indra, king of the gods. They explain that the demons (Daityas) have beaten all these gods, and now they humbly come to Vishnu for shelter.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-23.plain: Parashara, telling the story to his student Maitreya, says Vishnu then appeared before the gods, holding his conch, discus and mace and shining with power. The gods, led by Brahma, bowed low, their eyes trembling with awe, and began to praise him as Pundarikaksha, the lotus-eyed one.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-24.plain: The gods tell Vishnu that he is everything. He is Brahma, Shiva (holder of the bow Pinaka), Indra, Fire, Wind, Varuna, the Sun and Yama, and all the other gods too. Even the gods standing before him are really part of him, because he is in all things, including sacrifice itself.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-25.plain: The gods say Vishnu fills the whole universe, and some of him can be known and some cannot. Beaten by the demons, they ask him for his strength. They say that suffering, worry about enemies, confusion and misery go on only until a person turns to him for protection, so they beg for his grace.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-26.plain: Pleased, Vishnu (also called Hari) promises to make the gods strong again. He tells them to work with the demons to bring healing herbs to the Ocean of Milk. They should use Mount Mandara as a churning stick and the serpent Vasuki as the rope, and churn the ocean for amrita, the drink of immortality, with his help.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-27.plain: Vishnu tells the gods to make peace with the demons and ask for their help, promising them a share of the reward. The amrita will make the gods strong and immortal. But Vishnu says he will make sure the demons do the hard work and do not get the amrita.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-28.plain: The gods followed Vishnu's advice and made peace with the demons. Together they threw healing herbs into the white Ocean of Milk. Using Mount Mandara as the stick and Vasuki the serpent as the rope, they began to churn.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-29.plain: On Krishna's (Vishnu's) advice, the gods held the serpent's tail and the demons held its head. The fiery breath from Vasuki's head made the demons weak. Clouds blown by his breath rained on the tail end and refreshed the gods.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-30.plain: Vishnu took the form of a giant tortoise and held up the mountain from below in the middle of the ocean. He also took one form among the gods and another among the demons to help pull the serpent. In yet another huge form, which no one could see, he held the mountain from above.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-31.plain: Vishnu gave strength to the serpent and to the gods. As the churning went on, the first thing to rise was Surabhi, the holy cow who gives butter for offerings. Gods and demons alike were thrilled and stared at her.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-32.plain: Next came Varuni, goddess of wine, her eyes rolling as if drunk. Then rose the Parijata tree, filling the world with fragrance, followed by many beautiful Apsaras (heavenly dancers). Then the Moon came up, and Shiva (Maheshwara) took him.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-33.plain: The serpents took the poison that came up from the ocean. Then Dhanvantari, the divine healer, rose dressed in white, carrying a water pot full of amrita, and everyone was overjoyed. Then the goddess Sri (Lakshmi, goddess of fortune) rose, sitting on an open lotus and holding a lotus.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-34.plain: The great sages joyfully sang the Sri Sukta hymn to Lakshmi, and heavenly musicians sang before her. Heavenly dancers danced, the sacred rivers like the Ganga brought water to bathe her, and a great elephant poured water over her from golden pots.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-35.plain: The Ocean of Milk took a body and gave Lakshmi a garland of lotuses that never fade, and Vishwakarma, the divine craftsman, gave her jewels. Dressed and adorned, she went to Vishnu (Hari) in front of everyone and rested on his chest. When she looked at the gods, they suddenly felt great joy.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-36.plain: Lakshmi did not look at the demons, who always ignored Vishnu, and they grew very worried. The demons grabbed Dhanvantari's pot of amrita. Then Vishnu took the form of a beautiful woman, charmed them, got the pot back and gave it to the gods.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-37.plain: Indra (Sakra) and the gods drank the amrita. The demons attacked them with swords, but the gods, now strong, beat them back, and the demons fled to the underworld. Bowing to Vishnu, the gods again ruled the heavens.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-38.plain: After this, the Sun moved on its proper path again, and the stars and planets went back to their orbits. Fire burned brightly, and all creatures began to care about doing right. The three worlds were blessed again, and Indra shone with glory once more.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-39.plain: Back on his throne, Indra praised Lakshmi, the lotus-born mother of all beings who rests on Vishnu's chest. He said she is success, nectar, the sacred offering words, dawn and dusk, light, wealth, intelligence, faith and Saraswati, goddess of learning.

vishnu-purana-churning-1-9-40.plain: Indra goes on saying Lakshmi is every kind of knowledge: knowledge of sacrifice, of the soul, of God, logic, the three Vedas, farming and trade, and the rules of government. She gives freedom from rebirth, and the whole world is full of her gentle and fierce forms.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-9.plain: The cowherd women go on crying out that they cannot live without Krishna. He is so dear to them that even their mothers' homes would mean nothing without him. They notice that even while the snakes wrap around him, Krishna is still smiling at them.
themes: unable to live without a loved one
calm in the middle of danger

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-10.plain: Parashara, the narrator, says that Rama (Balarama, Krishna's older brother, son of Rohini) sees Nanda staring in shock and Yashoda about to faint. So Balarama reminds Krishna who he really is. He asks why Krishna, the god of gods, is acting like a helpless human. He says Krishna is the center of all creation, like the hub of a wheel.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-11.plain: Balarama says he himself is a part of Krishna, born as his older brother. The gods have also been born as cowherds to share in Krishna's life on earth. He asks why Krishna is ignoring his friends and family, who are now so sad.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-12.plain: Balarama ends by saying Krishna has played the part of a human child long enough. Now he should defeat this terrible poisonous snake.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-13.plain: Once Balarama reminds him of his true nature, Krishna smiles and slips free of the snakes' coils. He grabs Kaliya's middle head, pushes it down, and dances on it. Each time the serpent tries to lift a head, Krishna stamps it down again.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-14.plain: Krishna's dancing feet crush the snakes until they faint and spit up blood. Kaliya's wives see their husband hurt and bleeding, so they beg Krishna, called the Slayer of Madhu, for mercy.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-15.plain: Kaliya's wives say they now know Krishna is the supreme god. Even the gods cannot praise him enough, so how could they? Earth, sky, water, fire and air are only parts of him. Even holy hermits have failed to fully understand him.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-16.plain: The wives bow to Krishna as smaller than the smallest atom and larger than the largest thing. He was never born and can never be destroyed. They say he is not punishing Kaliya out of anger but to protect the world. They beg him, as the most forgiving one, to show pity.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-17.plain: The wives point out that Kaliya is weak compared to Krishna, who holds up the whole universe. Someone so great has no reason to fight someone so small. They ask Krishna, as an act of kindness, to give them back their dying husband.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-18.plain: Kaliya is worn out, but he also weakly asks Krishna to forgive him. He says Krishna has unmatched power and is beyond everything, so he cannot find words to praise him.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-19.plain: Kaliya asks how he could ever praise the one from whom all the gods came, including Brahma, Rudra (Shiva), Indra and others. The whole universe is only a small part of Krishna. Even Brahma cannot understand his nature.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-20.plain: Kaliya says Krishna is worshipped by the king of the gods, and by sages who picture him in their hearts during meditation. Kaliya cannot worship him properly, so he asks Krishna to be pleased with him out of mercy alone. He adds that serpents are crooked by nature.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-21.plain: Kaliya argues that he acted cruelly because he was born a snake, and God made every creature the way it is. He would deserve punishment only if he went against his nature. He says being punished by Krishna is actually a blessing.
themes: is it my fault how I was made

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-22.plain: Kaliya says Krishna has taken away all his strength and poison. He asks only to be allowed to live, and asks what Krishna wants him to do.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-23.plain: Krishna tells Kaliya to leave the lake at once and go to the sea with his family. He promises that Garuda, the eagle who hunts snakes, will not harm him once he sees Krishna's footprints on his head. Kaliya bows and leaves with his whole family.

vishnu-purana-kaliya-5-7-24.plain: When the snake is gone, the cowherds hug Krishna as if he had come back from the dead, and they cry happy tears. People are amazed that the river's water is clean again. They praise Krishna, and he returns home to Vraja.
themes: joy at a loved one's safe return

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-1.plain: Parashara says that while Krishna and Rama played in Vraja, the rainy season ended and autumn came, with lotuses in full bloom. Fish suffered in the heat, like a man worn down by selfish desires for his family. Peacocks fell silent, like hermits who give up worldly pleasures.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-2.plain: White clouds emptied of rain left the sky, like wise people leaving home after finding wisdom. Lakes dried up in the sun, like hearts dried up by selfishness. Still waters filled with white lilies, like pure minds that see the truth.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-3.plain: The moon shone brightly among the stars, like a saint near the end of life among good people. Rivers slowly drew back from their banks, like wise people slowly loosening their attachment to family. Swans came back to the lakes, like false hermits who slip back into worldly troubles.

vishnu-purana-govardhan-5-10-4.plain: The ocean grew calm, like a saint who has found deep peace through discipline. The waters became clear, like the minds of wise people who see Vishnu in everything. The cloudless sky was like a devotee's heart with its worries burned away. The cool moon eased the sun's heat, the way clear thinking eases the pain of pride.
